newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Mohajir leader urges calm following Bhutto sacking.
newsitem.headline: Mohajir leader urges calm following Bhutto sacking.

text.p: The exiled leader of Pakistan's Mohajir National Movement (MQM) on Tuesday urged his followers in Karachi to refrain from revenge attacks on security forces in the wake of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's ouster.

"I know you have suffered a lot at the hands of police, security agencies, and terrorists...but promise me you won't take revenge," Altaf Hussain said in a speech delivered by telephone from Britain and broadcast at MQM headquarters in central Karachi.

Hundreds of MQM workers gathered at the headquarters to hear Hussain. They cheered and danced to celebrate Bhutto's sacking earlier on Tuesday by President Farooq Leghari on charges of corruption and misrule.
Elsewhere in Karachi's central district, an MQM stronghold, witnesses said youths destroyed police pickets.

The MQM accuses security forces of summary killings of its workers in Karachi, where political and sectarian violence claimed more than 2,000 lives last year. Another 370 have died in the violence so far this year.
The MQM seeks greater political and economic rights for Mohajirs, Urdu-speaking Moslems who migrated from India when the during the partition in 1947.

"The Benazir Bhutto government is responsible for the extrajudicial killings of our workers, we demand President Farooq Leghari provide us justice," Hussain said, while asking supporters not to take the law into their own hands.
"We demand an end to the operation against the Mohajirs and a relief package for the victims," he said.
Bhutto's government had blamed the MQM for much of the bloodletting in Karachi.
"After a long time, there are smiles on our faces," one pro-MQM youngster said.
"They killed my son...I want them to be hanged," one woman said.
Witnesses said youths carrying MQM flags gathered in small groups on roads in eastern and central Karachi, chanting slogans in support of the MQM.
Police arrested two MQM workers and seized at least five vehicles, said Ishtiaq Azhar, MQM member of Pakistan's Senate.
The Shaheed Bhutto group, a dissident faction of Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party, also welcomed the government's dismissal.
Murtaza Bhutto, the ousted prime minister's estranged brother, was leader of the Shaheed Bhutto group until he was killed by police last month.
Shaheed Bhutto blamed the government for the killing while the former prime minister said it was a conspiracy against her family and her government.
"The dissolution of assemblies and ouster of this corrupt government was a demand of our martyred chairman Mir Murtaza Bhutto and we support the president's action," a faction spokesman told Reuters.
"We congratulate caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid and demand accountability for all corrupt officials and the arrest of the killers of Mir Murtaza," he said.
